docs.title: HMPL Documentation
docs.text:
This site is the published documentation for the HMPL repository.

Use the navigation to access: - Law (normative) - Whitepaper - Journal drafts - Regulator memo pack - Governance model - Reference architecture - Schemas and CXL

docs.title: HMPL vs Dubai’s Human–Machine Collaboration Icons (HMC)
docs.text:
Dubai’s Human–Machine Collaboration (HMC) Icons are a disclosure taxonomy: they label how much human vs machine contribution was involved in producing research or content, and where in the workflow the machine contributed (e.g., ideation, analysis, writing). They are designed for transparency and credibility in publications.

HMPL is different: it is a governance architecture and enforcement protocol for high‑stakes systems where machines can cause real‑world impact. HMPL defines two disjoint domains (Human judgment vs Machine execution), constrains what may cross the interface (“the Dash”), and mandates escalation/freeze, precedent-to-policy compilation, and auditable policy versioning.

Use them together: HMC to disclose collaboration, HMPL to constrain authority and execution.

docs.title: CXL Specification (Deterministic Boolean Constraints)
docs.text:
CXL is a deterministic, side-effect-free boolean expression language evaluated over frozen inputs (E,S,R,P,Y). It is designed to be structurally incapable of narrative and external calls.

Mandatory limits: - Max expression length: 2048 - Max AST nodes: 256 - Max quantifier iterations: 64 - Max regex length: 128 (RE2-safe subset) - Max string length in MATCH: 256

Error contract: Any runtime error MUST evaluate to false and set an eval_error flag.

docs.title: Authority Classes
docs.text: A2 Safety (tighten only), A3 Domain, A4 Sovereign (constitutional changes + monotonicity breaks).

docs.title: H-Ledger Model
docs.text: H-Ledger is append-only, hash-chained. Records governance events (policy publish, freeze, rollback), never user data or model outputs.

docs.title: Precedent → Policy Pipeline
docs.text: Capture → Sanitize → Compile → Verify → Ratify → Publish → Inject.

docs.title: Reference Architecture
docs.text: Dual-plane architecture: H-plane (ratification/signing) and A-plane (execution). Dash enforces schema-validated artifacts only.

docs.title: HMPL Implementation Repo Skeleton
docs.text:
A minimal, runnable reference implementation of HMPL v1.0+ primitives: - Schemas (Dash artifacts) - Validators (schema + hardening) - Lane Sentinel (escalation / freeze enforcement) - Policy Compiler (H-PREC → P-BNDL candidate) - Ledger Anchor (hash-chained governance event log)

This repo is intentionally behavior-agnostic: it does not “align” models, it enforces constitutional incapacity at the system boundary.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• schemas/ canonical JSON Schemas (hardened)
  • packages/common/ shared types + AJV validators + hardening guard
  • services/dash-gateway/ validates inbound/outbound Dash packets
  • services/lane-sentinel/ enforces Lane Change Law + IFP (freeze)
  • services/policy-compiler/ compiles H-PREC into P-BNDL candidate
  • services/ledger-anchor/ append-only hash-chained event log (H-Ledger stub)
  • tools/cxl/ tiny deterministic CXL evaluator (subset)

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Requirements: Node.js 20+

npm install
npm run build
npm run dev

Then: - Dash Gateway: http://localhost:8080/health - Lane Sentinel: http://localhost:8081/health - Policy Compiler: http://localhost:8082/health - Ledger Anchor: http://localhost:8083/health

docs.title: Demo flow (local)
docs.text:
1) Send an Event Packet to Dash Gateway:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/event -H "content-type: application/json" -d @examples/e-pkt.query.json | jq .

2) Ask Lane Sentinel to evaluate a Decision Packet with Risk + Constraints:

curl -s http://localhost:8081/v1/evaluate -H "content-type: application/json" -d @examples/eval.request.json | jq .

3) Compile a human precedent into a policy bundle candidate:

curl -s http://localhost:8082/v1/compile -H "content-type: application/json" -d @examples/h-prec.sample.json | jq .

4) Anchor a governance event hash into the H-Ledger stub:

curl -s http://localhost:8083/v1/anchor -H "content-type: application/json" -d @examples/anchor.sample.json | jq .

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The Ledger here is a local file-based hash chain to demonstrate the proof surface.
  • Replace services/ledger-anchor with your real ledger (public or regulator-accessible) while keeping the event shape identical.
  • The CXL engine is intentionally small; swap it for a formally verified engine if needed—never expand it to allow narrative.

docs.title: HMPL (arXiv Submission Wrapper)
docs.text:
Abstract: HMPL is a proposed constitutional governance framework that enforces design-time incapacity: artificial execution systems cannot internalize meaning or author law. HMPL separates Human judgment from Artificial execution, mandates escalation under ambiguity and irreversibility, and derives trust from cryptographic audit events.

Manuscript references: - Normative text: law/HMPL_v1.0.md - Whitepaper: whitepapers/HMPL_Whitepaper_v1.1.md

docs.title: Preamble
docs.text:
This law is established in response to the deployment of artificial systems in high-stakes domains where decisions carry irreversible consequences. The foundational architectural violation of contemporary artificial intelligence is the internalization of meaning, a practice that erodes human authority, diffuses accountability, and creates unprovable claims of safety.

The Human–Machine Parallel Law (HMPL) is therefore instituted to correct this violation. Its purpose is to establish a permanent, structural separation between the cognitive domains of human judgment and machine execution. This separation ensures that human sovereignty is preserved not by post-hoc control or behavioral alignment, but by the design-time incapacity of artificial systems to assume authority they are not constitutionally permitted to hold.

docs.title: 1.1 Cognitive Domain Definitions
docs.text:
The Human–Machine Parallel Law recognizes two disjoint cognitive domains. These domains are legally separate and may never be merged. The Human Cognitive Domain is the sole source of legitimate meaning within the system.

Human Cognitive Domain (H): The domain of judgment under ambiguity, value commitment, strategic intent, and final accountability. Artificial Cognitive Domain (A): The domain of deterministic transformation, constraint evaluation, state preservation, and execution under externally supplied law.

docs.title: 1.2 Definition of Meaning
docs.text: Meaning is formally defined as a semantic construct that resolves ambiguity through value judgment. By this definition, meaning is non-computable within the Artificial Cognitive Domain and is explicitly prohibited from residing within its internal state.

docs.title: 1.3 Core Axioms
docs.text:
1. Axiom 1: Cognitive Non-Fusion — The Human and Artificial domains are disjoint (H ∩ A = ∅) and must never collapse into one another.
  2. Axiom 2: Meaning Non-Residence — Meaning is explicitly prohibited from residing within the internal state of any system in the Artificial Domain.
  3. Axiom 3: Escalation Dominance — When an escalation condition is met, the only admissible action for the Artificial Domain is to escalate.

docs.title: 2.0 The Constitutional Architecture: Dual-Domain Governance
docs.text: HMPL is enforced through a dual-domain architecture connected only by a single constrained interface (“The Dash” / “Operational Spine”).

docs.title: 3.1 Admissible Interface Artifacts
docs.text:
• Facts (structured)
  • Constraints (structured)
  • Risk Indicators (structured)
  • Calibrated Confidence Scores (bounded)
  • Finalized Human Decisions (as versioned rules or signed precedents)

docs.title: 3.2 Inadmissible Interface Artifacts
docs.text:
• Narrative
  • Justification
  • Emotion
  • Intuition
  • Belief
  • Persuasive argumentation

docs.title: 3.3 The Lane Change Law
docs.text:
Mandatory A → H escalation when: - policy collision - confidence below threshold - value trade-off - irreversible impact possible

Permissible H → A ratification only when: - decision finalized and signed - rule/precedent versioned - exception codified as signed rule - responsibility formally acknowledged

docs.title: 4.1 Prohibited Training Objectives
docs.text:
• Human-like reasoning or moral explanation
  • Value inference or simulated empathy
  • Intent inference or guessing
  • Persuasion or plausibility maximization

docs.title: 4.2 Permitted Training Objectives
docs.text:
• Certainty classification and ambiguity detection
  • Rule collision detection and constraint satisfaction
  • State preservation and integrity
  • Correct and timely escalation triggering

docs.title: 4.3 The Memory and Precedent Law
docs.text: Memory is purely operational (state, not experience). Human precedent is stored externally and injected only as versioned, signed rules.

docs.title: 5.1 The Precedent-to-Policy Pipeline
docs.text: 1) Capture 2) Compile 3) Verify & Ratify 4) Publish & Inject

docs.title: 5.2 Authority Classes
docs.text: A2 Safety, A3 Domain, A4 Sovereign.

docs.title: 5.3 Safety Monotonicity Invariant
docs.text: Constraints tighten by default; relaxing requires A4 signature and ledger record.

docs.title: 6.1 Incident Freeze Protocol (IFP)
docs.text: Freeze + escalate; self-repair is prohibited.

docs.title: 6.2 Policy Rollback Protocol (PRP)
docs.text: Signed rollback to last certified bundle; quarantines newer bundles; re-entry requires tests + ratification.

docs.title: 7.0 The Audit Law (HMPL-A)
docs.text:
H-Ledger records events of law (hashes, signatures, versions) not content or cognition.

Trust guarantees: Proof of Obedience, Proof of Containment, Proof of Human Sovereignty.

docs.title: Pharma Analogy
docs.text:
Analogy (Regulator-Friendly)

Think of HMPL as an automated pharmaceutical factory. The factory (Machine) is incredibly fast and precise at mixing chemicals, but it has no understanding of what health is or why a medicine is needed. Those meaningful decisions—the recipes and the safety thresholds—are developed by scientists (Humans) in a separate lab. The only connection between the lab and the factory is a digital keypad. The scientist enters a code (the rule), and the factory executes it. If the factory's sensors detect an unknown chemical or a pressure spike (ambiguity), it doesn't try to guess a solution; it immediately shuts down all valves (freeze) and flashes a red light (escalate) for the scientist to intervene. Meaning—the "why" and the "should"—never enters the factory's pipes.

docs.title: Diagram Caption
docs.text: Figure X — HMPL as a controlled lab‑to‑factory pipeline. Human authorities operate in a separate judgment domain that produces signed policy bundles and exception precedents. The AI domain is an execution engine that consumes only structured state, constraints, risk flags, calibrated confidence, and signed rules through “the Dash.” When ambiguity, policy collision, or irreversible impact is detected, the AI domain cannot improvise: it freezes and escalates. Governance actions (policy publish, freeze/rollback, certifications) are recorded on the H‑Ledger as hashes and signatures—enabling independent verification of obedience, containment, and human sovereignty without exposing user data or model internals.

docs.title: Regulator Paragraph
docs.text: HMPL treats high‑stakes AI like an automated pharmaceutical factory: the machine is exceptionally fast at mixing chemicals and executing recipes, but it has no constitutional permission to “understand” health, ethics, or legitimacy. Those decisions live only with licensed human authorities who author signed rules and safety thresholds outside the machine. The only connection is a constrained interface that transmits structured state and signed policy—never narrative justification. If the system detects ambiguity, policy collision, low confidence, or an irreversible risk signal, it must freeze all execution lanes and escalate; guessing is a constitutional violation. In short: meaning and authority stay in human hands, execution stays in machine hands, and every change in governing policy is provable by signatures and hashes.

docs.title: HMPL Whitepaper v1.1 (post-JOLT tone)
docs.text:
HMPL is an institutional governance standard for AI systems used in high-stakes or regulated domains. It treats the internalization of meaning as an architectural violation and replaces behavioral oversight with design-time incapacity: the Artificial Domain cannot host meaning or author law.

HMPL enforces dual-domain governance (Human H vs Artificial A) joined only by a constrained interface (“Dash”) that transfers structured state and blocks narrative. When ambiguity, policy collision, or irreversibility arises, escalation is mandatory. Human decisions are compiled into signed, versioned policy bundles; policy evolution is controlled by authority classes and recorded as cryptographic audit events. Trust is based on proof, not explainability claims.
